context: Real-time streaming line chart with a main 60-second view and a 5-minute overview panel with brushable selection, displaying an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process — a tech demo / data visualization hybrid
first_impression: Clean, deliberately engineered chart with a muted TOL blue palette, gradient area fill, and a professional overview+brush panel that signals real design intent beyond a first-draft AI chart.
what_works: The color choice (TOL #4477AA instead of steelblue or schemeCategory10) is a deliberate, non-default signal of design taste, used consistently across the line, fill, active controls, and brush selection. The stats row with monospace bold values and the crosshair interaction with snap-to-point dot create satisfying information density without clutter.
what_doesnt: The overview panel at 100px feels too thin and its label ('5-minute overview (LTTB downsampled)') is 0.7rem gray text nearly invisible against the white background — a layout detail that undercuts an otherwise strong interaction pattern. The stats bar labels (Current, Min, Max) are in the same size and weight as surrounding text, missing a chance to establish a clearer typographic tier between label and value.
